findings.evidence: Repo precedent: every existing point-level declaration carries a point marker — `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsHomEquiv` (`CommHopfAlgCat/Yoneda.lean:32`), `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.PointRepresentation.*` (`Comodule/Morphism.lean:41`, `Comodule/Dual.lean:43`), `Comodule.pointsAction`, `Comodule.endOfPoint`, `Tannaka.fgPointSemisimplePartTensorIso` (`Tannaka/JordanDecomposition.lean:449`), `Tannaka.pointNatIso` (`ScalarExtension.lean:72`). By contrast the unqualified members of `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra` are about `H` itself: `antipode_comul_antidistrib` (`Algebra/HopfAlgebra/Antipode.lean:49`) and `conjugationAlgHom` (`AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean:29`).
findings.fix: Mark the point level in the name or namespace: either rename to `pointSemisimplePart`/`pointUnipotentPart`/`pointJordanDecomposition`, or nest the file's declarations in a sub-namespace such as `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.Point` so they read `Point.semisimplePart`. Update the `## Main declarations` list (lines 26-33) to match.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.semisimplePart` (also `unipotentPart`, line 65, and `jordanDecomposition`, line 71) are named as if they were attributes of the Hopf algebra `H`, but their argument is a `K`-valued point. `HopfAlgebra.semisimplePart` reads as the semisimple part of a Hopf algebra (a standard, different notion), and gives no way to tell it apart from `GeneralLinearGroup.semisimplePart` at a glance.

summary: Names track the existing GeneralLinearGroup Jordan API closely and no notation is introduced, but the three new definitions sit unqualified in `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra`, where every other declaration is about the Hopf algebra `H` itself or is explicitly marked as point-level.
